kitDescription: Admi is a Wind SR Supporter whose Burst II is the core of her kit: when she casts, all allies (herself included) gain 50.91% Reload Speed and 28.34% Critical Damage for 10 seconds, and her cast lands just before the Full Burst window so both buffs cover it. Her Skill 1 is a defensive trigger: after she has been attacked 20 times, the whole team gains 9.59% Charge Damage Multiplier for 20 seconds, which scales the base charge damage of charge-weapon allies. Her Skill 2 is purely protective, cutting damage received by the two highest-final-ATK allies by 28.65% for 10 seconds. She has no self-damage lines, no DoT, no stacks, and no weapon swap — she is a pure team buffer whose value flows through faster reloads (more shots) and stronger crits.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas: all six kit lines are FAITHFUL (both burst lines) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (both S1 lines, both S2 lines), each gap carrying verbatim prose + ⚑ with estimate, recipe, and tier. The burst block converged four ways (driver = S2b = S5 = S6, byte-identical vs S6) and discriminates in both directions (fullBurstEnter re-keying, excludeSelf, matched-hit major-bucket arithmetic, reload shot-economy arm). The S5 RED is a single posture divergence, not a misread: S5 assumed S1 would ship as a modeled block; the driver ships it unmodeled because no attacked-count primitive exists and any interval stand-in invents an unmeasured cadence — a decision documented, formula-confirmed (scope lock has no incoming-damage channel), and consistent with the noise/yulha precedent, with the driver's phantom-S1/S2 arms proving the absence pins have teeth. Nothing must change for GO. Owner spot-checks for the same-model residual: (1) 'Charge Damage Multiplier ▲' → chargeDamageMultPct rests on the helm-wording inference agreed by all four agents, never confirmed against an in-game popup — worth one popup screenshot before a trigger primitive ever lands; (2) burstCast-over-fullBurstEnter is also a four-agent consensus (strongly supported by the kit's lack of a full-burst clause and the pre-FB cast timing, and discriminated by test, but still single-family reasoning); (3) S2b preferred an interval-⚑ over full unmodeling for S1 — if boss attack cadence is ever measured, revisit encoding S1 as a measured interval rather than leaving it dark, since real-fight uptime is plausibly near-permanent.
